_comment: An EXAMPLE, not live configuration. Managed settings are deployed to a machine by an administrator and are not overridable from a repository — which is the whole point of them, and the reason this file sits in docs/ rather than in .claude/. Copy it to the managed settings path for the platform, adjust, and deploy. See code.claude.com/docs/en/settings and code.claude.com/docs/en/admin-setup.
_what_this_is_for: The team settings in .claude/settings.json are a convenience: they make the common commands quiet and wire the hooks. They are also editable by anybody who can open a pull request. Where that is not acceptable — a regulated environment, an audited pipeline, a machine that holds credentials for something that matters — the same rules are stated here instead, where the agent and the repository both inherit them and neither can widen them.

permissions._comment: The safe inner loop, and nothing else. Everything not named here asks. A build, a test, a lint and reading the tree is the whole loop this repository needs to work in.

_bypass: Without this, every rule above is one keystroke from being irrelevant.

sandbox._comment: Filesystem and network confinement. The allowlist is the toolchain and the registry: an operating system that builds offline is the goal, and every host on this list is a step away from it.

credentials._comment: Blocked outright rather than merely unread. A session that cannot reach these cannot leak them, and cannot be talked into using them by something it read in a file.

_managed_only: Each of these closes a route by which the rules above stop applying: a local settings file that widens permissions, a hook added on the machine, a flag on the command line, an MCP server nobody reviewed, a marketplace nobody vetted, a version predating a fix.
_allowManagedHooksOnly_note: false on purpose. This repository's guardrails ARE repository hooks — .claude/hooks/ is reviewed like code and tested by .claude/hooks/selftest.sh in CI. Setting this to true would disable them and leave only the managed set, which is a net loss unless the managed set reimplements them. Decide deliberately; do not copy this line without reading it.
_audit: Sessions, tool calls and hook decisions are retrievable through the Compliance API — platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-api. The release gate prints its authorisation string on every allowed crossing so that the transcript carries the record, and that is the artifact an audit asks for.
